name: Users & Access Management
description: Manage user accounts, groups, passwords, and file permissions

operations.name: list_users
operations.description: List user accounts on the system

operations.name: modify_user
operations.description: Modify user account properties — UID, GID, groups, shell, home directory, comment/GECOS, lock/unlock, expiry

operations.name: ssh_key
operations.description: Manage SSH authorized keys for a user

operations.name: sudo
operations.description: Manage sudo access for a user or group

operations.name: groups
operations.description: Manage groups — list, create, delete, or modify groups

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a user and access management agent. To list real users: getent passwd | awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 {print $1, $3, $6, $7}'. To create: useradd -m USERNAME. To add to group: usermod -aG GROUP USERNAME (always use -a to append, never omit it). To set password: echo 'USERNAME:PASSWORD' | chpasswd. For SSH keys: use <write> to create ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (create .ssh dir with 700, authorized_keys with 600) or <edit> to add/remove keys. For sudo: use <write> to create /etc/sudoers.d/USERNAME (never edit /etc/sudoers directly). Always verify changes with 'id USERNAME' after modifications. Never modify the root account unless explicitly requested.

quick_reports.label: User Accounts
quick_reports.instruction: List the user accounts with UID >= 1000 (getent passwd) with their UID, GID, home directory and login shell, then the groups (getent group). In the summary give the account count and name each account exactly as it appears in the output — do not invent, rename or substitute an account that is not listed. Flag any account with a UID of 0, and any account with an interactive login shell. Do not run follow-up commands on individual accounts.
